major.name: Political Science - BS - Data Analytics
narrative: All courses taken for a political science major must be taken for a letter grade and a grade of C- or better must be earned.
Lower-division courses POLI 27, POLI 28, POLI 40, POLI 197I, and POLI 197SD may not be used to satisfy requirements in the political science major or minor.
Students may not receive credit for both POLI 5 and POLI 5D; for both POLI 10 and POLI 10D; for both 11 and 11D; 12 and 12D; 13 and 13D; 30 and 30D.

Two upper-division courses in a field may be substituted for that field's lower-division course. However, these courses cannot also be used to satisfy the upper-division course requirements for a concentration of that field.
At least ten courses in political science must be taken in residence at UC San Diego. A total maximum of six courses may be taken elsewhere and applied toward the major.
Students must maintain an overall 2.0 GPA in the major.
Courses taken to satisfy requirements for the major may not be taken Pass/Not Pass with the exception of a maximum of two independent study courses (POLI 199).

Students who pass the Advanced Placement (AP) Tests in American or Comparative Politics may petition to be exempted from taking POLI 10 or 10D or 11 or 11D (respectively) ... students must pass with a score of 5.
Law and Society 101, Contemporary Legal Issues, may be used in fulfilling the twelve upper-division course requirement for the political science major.

Data analytics majors must satisfy the following sixteen courses: POLI 5D, Data Analytics for the Social Sciences; POLI 30D, Political Inquiry; two of the following four lower-division courses (POLI 10 or 10D, 11 or 11D, 12 or 12D, and 13 or 13D) and twelve upper-division courses. (The concentration listing itself reads 'POLI 5 or 5D' and 'POLI 30 or 30D'.)
POLI 5D is allowable only for the data analytics major.

nodes.title: Data Analytics for the Social Sciences
nodes.description: (Cross-listed with POLI 5D.) Students engage in hands-on learning with applied social science problems. The course teaches the basics of data management and collection, data analysis, and data visualization. To perform these analyses, students learn how to code in various programming software, including Excel, Stata, and R. Students may receive credit for only one of the following courses: ECON 5, POLI 5, POLI 5D, ECON 5R.

nodes.title: Introduction to Political Science: American Politics
groups: Lower-division requirements: Two other lower-division courses
nodes.description: This course surveys the processes and institutions of American politics. Among the topics discussed are individual political attitudes and values, political participation, voting, parties, interest groups, Congress, presidency, Supreme Court, the federal bureaucracy, and domestic and foreign policy making. POLI 10 is Lecture only, and POLI 10D is Lecture plus Discussion section. These courses are equivalents of each other in regard to major requirements, and students may not receive credit for both 10 and 10D.

nodes.title: Political Inquiry
nodes.description: Introduction to the logic of inference in social science and to quantitative analysis in political science and public policy including research design, data collection, data description and computer graphics, and the logic of statistical inference (including linear regression). POLI 30 is Lecture only, and POLI 30D is Lecture plus Discussion section. These courses are equivalents of each other in regard to major requirements, and students may not receive credit for both 30 and 30D.

nodes.title: Social Networks
nodes.description: This class explores the many ways in which face-to-face social networks have a powerful effect on a wide range of human behaviors. With a foundation in understanding real-world networks, we can then consider how these networks function online.

nodes.title: Data Analysis and United States Politics
nodes.description: This course examines U.S. politics from a computational point of view. Through in-class work and hands-on assignments, we will use data analysis tools to collect, analyze, and visualize data related to various facets of federal level politics in the US. Students will develop statistical and computational skills that will assist them in advanced analyses of elections, legislative outcomes, lobbying, and other dynamics of the lawmaking process in Congress.

nodes.title: Economic Theories of Political Behavior
nodes.description: An introduction to theories of political behavior developed with the assumptions and methods of economics. General emphasis will be upon theories linking individual behavior to institutional patterns. Specific topics to be covered will include collective action, leadership, voting, and bargaining.

nodes.title: Policy Assessment
nodes.description: The use of real data to assess policy alternatives. Introduction to benefit/cost analysis, decision theory, and the valuation of public goods. Applications to health, environmental, and regulatory economic policy making.

nodes.title: Algorithms, Public Policy, and Ethics
nodes.description: The deployment of predictive algorithms for public policy optimization has increased in recent years across a variety of domains. This course will introduce key concepts, considerations, and concerns relating to algorithmic decision-making in policy processes. This includes understanding how data are used to make predictions, how predictions can be used to aid decision-making, the conditions under which these practices will be effective, and the important ethical dimensions of these practices.

nodes.title: Applied Data Analysis for Political Science
nodes.prereq_text: POLI 30 or POLI 30D or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This course is an advanced introductory course for undergraduates. It will acquaint students with statistical methodology as it is used in the social sciences. It is assumed that the student has the mathematical background to progress through the materials a bit faster than in a true introductory course.

nodes.title: Making Policy with Data
nodes.prereq_text: POLI 5 or 5D or ECON 5 and POLI 30 or 30D.
nodes.description: This class explores how we can make policy recommendations using data. We attempt to establish causal relationships between policy intervention and outcomes based on statistical evidence. Hands-on examples will be provided throughout the course.

nodes.title: Advanced Social Data Analytics
nodes.prereq_text: POLI 5 or 5D or ECON 5 and POLI 30 or 30D.
nodes.description: An accelerated course in computer programming and data analytics for collecting, analyzing, and understanding data in the social world. Students engage in hands-on learning with applied social science problems, developing statistical and computational skills for sophisticated data manipulation, analysis, visualization.

nodes.title: Social Network Analysis
nodes.description: This class introduces tools for analyzing social networks including graph visualization, egocentric and sociocentric network measures, network simulation, and data management.

nodes.title: Analyzing Elections
nodes.description: This course is concerned with the political economy of elections. It will analyze key topics in political science using both theoretical and empirical tools. Specific topics covered include party and candidate strategy, electoral campaigns, the role and origins of parties, electoral accountability, and voter behavior.

nodes.title: Machine Learning for Social Scientists
nodes.prereq_text: CCS 1 or ECON 5/5R or POLI 5/5D/5R/5DR or POLI 30/30D.
nodes.description: This course focuses on statistical and algorithmic techniques to analyze and utilize large collections of data for social science inferences. The goal of the course is to introduce students to modern machine learning methods and provide the skills necessary to apply the methods widely. In achieving this goal, students will learn about core concepts in machine learning and statistics, developing skills that are transferable to other types of data and inference problems.

nodes.title: Text as Data
nodes.prereq_text: POLI/ECON 5D or POLI 30D or POLI 170A or POLI 171 or POLI 172.
nodes.description: (Cross-listed with DSC 161.) This class explores statistical and computational methods to enable students to use text as a data source in the social sciences. Hands-on examples will equip students to work with text data in final projects.

nodes.title: Data Analysis for Policy Advice
nodes.description: This course is aimed at students interested in using their analytical skills to provide insights to decision-makers primarily in the government and nonprofit sectors. We will study the types of decision-makers that exist, what kinds of questions they typically have, the methods and data that are available to answer them, and how to go about packaging and delivering policy advice. These skills are taught using applied examples from public policy and administrative datasets.

nodes.title: Applied Data Analytics for United States National Security
nodes.description: Policymakers want analysts to have X-Men powers: read the minds of others, influence their behavior, and predict the future. This course surveys cutting-edge technologies and research methods used for data analytics roles in American foreign policy/intelligence. Students will be expected to replicate at least one quantitative study.

nodes.title: Special Topics in Political Science Methodology
nodes.description: Special topics course in quantitative methods for political science and broader social sciences. May be taken for credit up to three times.
